conversation.content: Can you provide me with a tailored plan to pay off my student loans?

message.content:
I can — but to make a tailored, realistic plan I need a few details about your loans and finances. Please provide as much of the following as you’re comfortable sharing (you can give ranges if you prefer):

Loan information
- Total student loan balance (all loans combined)
- Types of loans (federal, private, mix)
- For federal loans: breakdown by plan if you know it (Direct Subsidized/Unsubsidized, PLUS, Perkins), or at least whether you’re on standard/IBR/IBR/REPAYE/PAYE etc.
- Interest rates for each loan or an approximate average interest rate
- Minimum monthly payment for each loan (or total minimum payment)
- Grace period status (in repayment, in deferment/forbearance, in grace)

Income and household
- Your gross monthly (or annual) income and net take-home pay
- Household size and whether you file taxes jointly (affects federal repayment plans and forgiveness)
- Any irregular income (freelance, seasonal, bonuses)

Monthly budget and obligations
- Monthly housing cost (rent/mortgage)
- Other fixed monthly bills (utilities, insurance, car payment)
- Minimum monthly credit card or other debt payments
- Savings (emergency fund balance)
- Any assets you could use (cash, investments) and whether you want to keep an emergency fund

Goals and preferences
- Target timeline to be debt-free (e.g., 2 years, 5 years, 10 years)
- Risk tolerance (prefer predictable stable payments vs. aggressive payoff)
- Priority between paying down high-interest loans first vs. keeping cash/liquidity
- Interest in refinancing (private refinance) or public service/teacher loan forgiveness programs

Once you share the above (or as much as you want), I’ll build a tailored repayment plan covering:
- Which loans to prioritize (avalanche vs. snowball) and why
- Monthly payment targets and a payoff schedule with estimated payoff dates
- Options to lower monthly payments (income-driven repayment, consolidation, deferment) if needed
- Whether refinancing makes sense and what to watch for
- Steps to protect or accelerate progress (emergency fund, budgeting tips, bonus/apply windfalls)
- If applicable, guidance on forgiveness programs and paperwork to pursue them

If you’d rather not share numbers, I can give a general step-by-step template for common situations (recent grad, high-balance federal loans, mixed private/federal, low income), but it won’t be personalized. Which do you prefer?
